items.claim: Applying a theme puts the header band back to the shape's stroke color when the new theme names none
setThemeValue writes values the theme checker rejects, so the document falls back to `night`
items.note: No rule existed, so I made the strict call: it throws a `RangeError` on any value `diagramThemeErrors` refuses at that path. Recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: Applying a theme keeps the old theme's connector markers and trim
items.note: `LineField` gains `markerStart`, `markerEnd` and `trim`, and markers or a trim set in an edge's `colors` are recorded as owned. The changeset is `minor` because adding those names is new API.

items.claim: Applying a theme turns a requirement diagram's dashed connectors solid
items.note: No rule existed, so I made the call: a connector's dash, markers and trim follow a theme only while they are still what the previous theme drew. This also keeps an entity-relationship diagram's crow's feet, which cc639714f0 alone would have stripped. Recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: Applying a theme draws a container that names a theme role in the plain container colors
items.note: The container's role is now written into its trait, which the scene reader already expected, and the theme apply picks a region's colors the same way the builder does (`dataRegionStyle`).

items.claim: An off-page tag's box keeps its old size when a theme changes the label font
items.note: The apply now re-measures the box with `offPageTagSize`, the function that sizes a new tag.

items.claim: Applying a theme adds a fill to lanes that building never gave them
items.note: No rule existed, so I made the call: lanes built from data now get their theme's striped lane-body fills, as a theme apply and `addLane` already gave them. The draw-style XML writer and the DOT/Mermaid writer stopped stripping lane fills. Recorded in `docs/unruled.md`. Round 46 had ruled the XML writer's missing lane fill "not a defect", because building gave lanes no fill; that is now reversed.
duplicate of the setThemeValue finding from A, fixed bb81e4fcdf

items.claim: Applying a theme drops widths and dashes, it keeps only colors
items.note: The builders and the theme write now share one `outlineOf` rule. A width or dash set in an item's own `colors` is recorded in a new `ownLine` trait field and kept.

items.claim: Style edits on a sequence part never show, or are lost at the next redraw
items.note: `diagramStyleOf` now returns `null` for a sequence and its parts, so the style edits leave them alone.

items.claim: Style edits throw partway through on a locked node
items.note: Question: no rule existed, so I made the call. Locked shapes, connectors and text rows are skipped and the rest are edited, as `applyDiagramTheme` already does. The call is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`; throwing up front on any locked id was the alternative.

items.claim: A hand fill sends header text to the fill even when the theme names a `headerText`
items.note: `diagramScene` and the theme write already used `headerText`; `setDiagramColor` was the odd one out. `setDiagramColor` gains a `theme` option, so its changeset is `minor`.

items.claim: `diagramThemeFrom` takes any object with a `roles` key unchecked
items.note: It now checks with `diagramThemeErrors` and caches the result per value. A theme that fails falls back, with one development warning per value.

items.claim: The theme-file check skips optional fields, non-finite sizes and an empty `series`
`setThemeValue` makes partial roles and sparse arrays
items.note: Question: no rule existed, so I made the strict call. It now throws `RangeError` on a role, lane body or series index the theme lacks; appending one color at the end of `series` is still allowed. Recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.
A token that doesn't parse as a color falls back to `paper`'s.

items.claim: A text row clamped at size 1 doesn't come back on a theme round trip
items.note: The size the step couldn't take is kept on the row's data as `unclampedFontSize`, and the next step moves from it. Setting the size by hand clears it.

items.claim: The `defaultRole` doc contradicts what connectors do
items.note: Doc-only, so no test and no changeset.
